title: Nvidia reportedly halts GeForce RTX 5090 production in favor of AI data center and professional GPUs — impending supply drought expected to drive up prices, RTX 5080 24GB rumored as new gaming flagship
key_facts: Nvidia has reportedly stopped selling its GB202 graphics processors for GeForce RTX 5090 cards, including the 'D' variants for China, per a leaked notice from an unknown factory cited by the leaker @hongxing2020.
A second leaker, @Zed__Wang, confirmed the report and said GB202 silicon will in future be used only on data center and professional graphics cards.
The notice also says the top GeForce card will become the RTX 5080 24GB and the RTX 5080 16GB will be discontinued.
Tom's Hardware calls this unverified and not an official Nvidia announcement; Nvidia had not responded to a request for comment.
Tom's Hardware's own analysis: Nvidia can earn far more from GB202 chips in professional cards (the RTX 6000 Pro with 96 GB of memory can sell for around $15,000) than in the RTX 5090.
RTX 5090 cards are unlikely to vanish at once because partners and retailers hold stock, but availability would decline and prices would be affected.
Next-generation Rubin-based RTX 60-series cards are rumored not to arrive until late 2027 or even 2028.
quote_evidence: This is, of course, an unverified claim and not an official Nvidia announcement.
Even if Nvidia has indeed discontinued shipments of GB202 processors for consumer graphics cards, GeForce RTX 5090 boards are unlikely to disappear from the market overnight.
Typically, Nvidia does not comment on rumors.
why_it_matters_hint: If true, the fastest consumer graphics card would become scarcer and dearer while Nvidia puts limited chip supply into higher-priced AI and professional products.
event_date: Leak reported 10 Oct 2026; no official Nvidia announcement.
notes: Rumor from an unnamed factory notice shared by leakers on X; Nvidia had not commented. The article ends with a buy-now remark, which is advice and is not used.
